title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: tbl.now provides tbl_now S3 class: tibble extension epidemiological nowcasting carries two time indices — event_date (something happened) report_date (recorded) — plus modelling metadata (strata, covariates, temporal effects, now, units, data type). fully dplyr-compatible. tbl.now data-structure + specification layer, modelling engine. standardises/validates data stores lazy specs; actual nowcasting done downstream diseasenowcasting. also ships model-free diagnostics — autoplot(), reporting-delay drift / change-point tests, batch (backlog-dump) detection — exploring data model chosen (experimental). Every tbl_now auto-computes three protected numeric columns: Removing protected column downgrades object back plain tibble (warning). Protected columns also include event_date, report_date, case_count (count types).
code: library(tbl.now) library(dplyr)

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: event_date/report_date accept tidy-select (bare names strings). Units data type inferred default ("auto"). Useful arguments: now = — “-” date nowcast. Defaults max(report_date). event_units / report_units — "days" | "weeks" | "months" | "years" | "numeric"; "auto" infers spacing. report_units must coarser equal event_units. align_weeks = TRUE — weekly data, snaps dates .delay integer (see ). may pass .delay + one date instead dates; missing date reconstructed. Always check worked:
code: # Linelist — one row per observed case (no counts column) tn <- tbl_now(   denguedat,   event_date  = onset_week,      # or "onset_week"   report_date = report_week,   strata      = gender,   verbose     = FALSE )  # Count data — one row per (event, report[, strata]) with a counts column tn <- tbl_now(   mpoxdat,   event_date  = dx_date,   report_date = dx_report_date,   case_count  = n,               # REQUIRED for count data types   strata      = race,   data_type   = "count-incidence",   verbose     = FALSE ) is_tbl_now(tn)            # TRUE validate_tbl_now(tn)      # errors if invalid tn                        # print() shows the footer with all attributes

what: Skill: tell which data type a dataset is
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Three data types: find , build data_type = "auto" read back: inference heuristic (infer_data_type): case_count column → "linelist". decrease → "count-incidence" (incremental counts go ); monotonically non-decreasing → "count-cumulative". auto guess wrong (e.g. genuinely cumulative data happens never decrease small sample), pass data_type = explicitly.
code: get_data_type(tn)

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Conversions two count types go ways; can never rebuild linelist: Supported: linelist→incidence, linelist→cumulative, incidence→cumulative, cumulative→incidence, re-aggregation within type. cumulative → incidence de-accumulates: within event date (× grouping), ordered report date, increment cumulative total minus previous one. cumulative totals can revised downward, increment can negative — legitimate net -revision, delay diagnostics drop non-positive weights. (autoplot() etc. now work count-cumulative data FluSight.) downstream model needing non-negative increments — e.g. tbl_now_to_baselinenowcast() — still refuses cumulative input. supported (errors): count-* → linelist (un-count aggregated data). might need individual records, keep linelist. Pre-aggregation automatic. Every function needs incidence calls to_count() first, groups (event_date, report_date, .event_num, .report_num, strata, is_censored, covariates, temporal-effect cols) sums counts — extra column declare stratum summed away, plotted. (column like race present stratum, rows correctly collapsed.) tbl_now extra columns prints non-uniqueness warning construction flag .
code: to_count(x, to = "count-incidence") to_count(x, to = "count-cumulative") linelist  ──►  count-incidence  ◄──►  count-cumulative

what: Skill: initial vs latest reported cases
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Two views “many cases occurred event_date”: get_initial_reported_cases = first observed event date (naive, -incomplete incidence). get_latest_reported_cases = best current estimate given everything reported now. de-facto “truth far” used plotting observed epidemic curve scoring nowcasts. get_nth_reported_cases(tn, delay) = cumulative count event date using reports delay ≤ delay (report units). delay = 0 initial snapshot (cases reported delay 0); delay = 1 adds delay-1 reports; delay = Inf (maximum delay) equals get_latest_reported_cases(). Use reconstruct reporting triangle “observed delay periods event”. three return count-cumulative-style tbl_now collapsed one row per event_date (× strata). gap initial latest exactly nowcast predicts.
code: get_initial_reported_cases(tn)   # the FIRST reported count per event_date get_latest_reported_cases(tn)    # the MOST-RECENT reported count per event_date get_nth_reported_cases(tn, delay = 2)   # cumulative count observed within delay <= 2

what: Skill: add / change / remove strata and covariates
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: strata = variables nowcast computed separately (age group, sex, region). covariates = predictors may improve nowcast (e.g. weather), split-. accept tidy-select. Adders append, changers replace whole set, removers drop: strata/covariate column must exist data. Strata integer, character, factor.
code: # strata tn <- add_strata(tn, age_group, region)   # append tn <- change_strata(tn, sex)              # replace the strata set with just `sex` tn <- remove_strata(tn, region)           # drop one tn <- remove_all_strata(tn)  # covariates tn <- add_covariates(tn, humidity) tn <- change_covariates(tn, temperature, humidity) tn <- remove_covariates(tn, temperature) tn <- remove_all_covariates(tn)  get_strata(tn);     get_num_strata(tn) get_covariates(tn); get_num_covariates(tn)

what: Skill: mark whether data is right-censored
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: is_censored flags reports arrive artificial batches representing right-censoring rather true reporting dynamics (e.g. lab outage week reports land later day). is_censored attribute stores name logical column (TRUE/FALSE per row). tell whether dataset censored: .null(get_is_censored(tn)) → TRUE means censoring indicator set. censoring column must logical validate_tbl_now() rejects .
code: df <- df |> mutate(was_batched = report_date == as.Date("2021-03-15")) tn <- tbl_now(df, event_date = onset, report_date = reported,               is_censored = was_batched, verbose = FALSE)  # or after creation: tn <- add_is_censored(tn, was_batched)     # errors if one is already set tn <- change_is_censored(tn, was_batched)  # replace (pass NULL to clear) tn <- remove_is_censored(tn)  get_is_censored(tn)   # column name, or NULL if not censored

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Temporal effects (calendar covariates Fourier seasonality) stored lazily spec, materialised columns demand. add_temporal_effects() can called repeatedly (appends specs); can mix date_type = "event_date" "report_date". Seasonality / Fourier: seasons cycle periods. daily data weekly seasonality use seasons = 52, season_length = 7 (period = 364 days); season_length defaults 1 (period = seasons). -holiday / -weekend lags (capture rebound break): holiday_lags = N / weekend_lags = N non-negative integer depths materialise indicator columns ..._holiday_lag_1 … _N ..._weekend_lag_1 … _N, flagging dates exactly k working days holiday / weekend (weekends holidays skipped counting, effect lands first day back work). holiday_lags requires holidays calendar. Best daily data. Replace clear: Order matters: compute_temporal_effects() add_temporal_effects() -op. replace_temporal_effects() removes computed columns — call compute_temporal_effects() afterward.
code: # 1) build a spec spec <- temporal_effects(   day_of_week   = FALSE,   weekend       = FALSE,   day_of_month  = FALSE,   month_of_year = TRUE,   week_of_year  = TRUE,   holiday_lags  = 0,            # after-HOLIDAY effect (see below); needs `holidays`   weekend_lags  = 0,            # after-WEEKEND effect (see below)   seasons       = integer(0),   # Fourier periods, e.g. c(7, 52, 365)   season_length = 1,            # multiply each season; period = seasons * season_length   holidays      = NULL          # an almanac::rcalendar(), see next skill )  # 2) attach (NO columns created yet). date_type = "event_date" (default) or "report_date" tn <- add_temporal_effects(tn, spec, date_type = "event_date")  # 3) materialise the columns when ready for modelling tn <- compute_temporal_effects(tn, overwrite = FALSE)  get_temporal_effects(tn)       # list of specs (length 0 = none attached) get_temporal_effect_cols(tn)   # character(0) before compute; column names after tn <- replace_temporal_effects(tn, temporal_effects(week_of_year = TRUE))  # drops old computed cols tn <- remove_temporal_effects(tn)                                          # clears spec + cols

what: Skill: calendar effects for ANY country (custom almanac holidays)
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Holidays use almanac package (v1.0). temporal_effects(holidays = ...) accepts almanac_rcalendar. restrict almanac::cal_us_federal() — build calendar recurring rules rholiday(rschedule, name) rcalendar(). Building blocks: yearly(), monthly(), weekly() recurrence rules refined recur_on_day_of_month(), recur_on_month_of_year(), recur_on_day_of_week(), etc.; wrap rule rholiday(); combine rcalendar(). almanac Suggests — install missing.
code: library(almanac)  # A fixed-date holiday: Mexican Independence Day, every Sep 16 indep <- yearly() |>   recur_on_month_of_year("Sep") |>   recur_on_day_of_month(16)  # Combine custom + built-in holidays into one calendar mx_calendar <- rcalendar(   rholiday(indep, "Mexican Independence Day"),   hol_new_years_day(),   hol_christmas() )  # Sanity-check which dates are holidays almanac::alma_in(as.Date(c("2023-09-16", "2023-12-25", "2023-06-01")), mx_calendar) #> TRUE TRUE FALSE  # Use it as a temporal effect tn <- tn |>   add_temporal_effects(temporal_effects(holidays = mx_calendar)) |>   compute_temporal_effects()

what: Skill: which dplyr verbs to use (and which to avoid)
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: tbl_now implements dplyr generics attributes survive data manipulation: Rules thumb: ✅ Use filter, select, mutate, arrange, group_by/ungroup, rename freely — temporal-effects spec attributes preserved dplyr never triggers temporal-effect computation. ⚠️ remove protected columns (.event_num, .report_num, .delay, event_date, report_date, case_count) via select()/mutate(... = NULL) — downgrades plain tibble warning. Removing strata covariate column instead silently drops attribute. ❌ rowwise() supported — behaviour undefined; avoid . non-trivial pipe, confirm is_tbl_now(x) handing object diseasenowcasting.

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: autoplot() (ggplot2 generic, re-exported tbl.now) returns multi-panel patchwork diagnostic. ggplot2 hard dependency; patchwork Suggests (install ). Two panel families. Case-count panels: Empirical delay distribution ("delay_distribution") — case-count-weighted histogram .delay. Observed epidemic process ("epidemic") — get_latest_reported_cases() event_date, dashed vertical incompleteness line now - quantile(delay, level). Holidays temporal-effects spec marked dots. Calendar effect ("calendar_weekday", "calendar_week", "calendar_month") — normalized boxplots (cases ÷ overall mean, 1 = average). Seasonality periodogram ("seasonality") — dominant peak suggests Fourier seasons length. Reporting-delay panels — inspect delay effects (delay patterned?): Delay calendar effect ("delay_weekday", "delay_week", "delay_month") — boxplots normalized mean reporting delay (mean delay ÷ overall mean delay, 1 = average) calendar group. Delay periodicity periodogram ("delay_seasonality") — cycle delay (e.g. weekly reporting rhythm). calendar/delay panels appear depends unit: daily → day--week week--year; weekly → week--year; monthly → month--year. (daily data week--year box legitimately summarizes ~7 daily values — stratification artefact.) Key arguments: level delay quantile incompleteness line drawn; 0.95 typical choice (“dates still missing ≥5% eventual counts incomplete”). autoplot() works three data types, including count-cumulative (de-accumulates internally).
code: library(tbl.now) autoplot(tn)                       # bare call works after library(tbl.now) autoplot(   tn,   panels = "all",         # "all" (default) | "calendar" | "delay_calendar" |                           #   a vector of concrete panel keys above.                           #   A SINGLE key returns a plain ggplot (not a patchwork).   by_strata = FALSE,      # TRUE => split every panel by stratum (dodged boxes /                           #   coloured lines / dodged bars, viridis, per-stratum                           #   normalization). Errors if no strata are set.   strata = NULL,          # which strata columns to group on when by_strata=TRUE                           #   (default = the object's strata; pass a subset)   level = 0.95,           # completeness threshold for the incompleteness line   delay_distribution_xlim = c(0, 10),   # per-panel x limits (all optional)   event_date_xlim = as.Date(c("2020-01-01","2020-12-31")),   calendar_effect_xlim = NULL,   seasonality_xlim = c(0, 60),   palette = .tbl_now_palette()          # override colours )  autoplot(tn, panels = "delay_week")     # just one panel -> a ggplot you can + to autoplot(tn, by_strata = TRUE)          # one fan of panels per stratum

what: Skill: diagnose reporting-delay drift & change points
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Ask whether reporting delay stable time trusting fixed delay model. experimental index event date. plot_delay_drift() — solid = rolling median, dashed = rolling mean, bands = 25–75% / 10–90%. window defaults 7 periods (7 days daily, 7 weeks weekly). recent, -yet-complete region (level incompleteness cutoff) shaded grey — read drift. changepoint = TRUE marks estimated median change point. Supports by_strata. test_delay_drift() returns tidy tibble (per stat × stratum) Kendall tau, Sen’s slope, p_value drift verdict; method "hamed-rao" (default), "yue-pilon" "block-bootstrap". Tests location ("median"/"mean") dispersion ("iqr"/"spread") statistic — drift can either. Runs mature data (mature_only = TRUE). test_delay_changepoint() returns estimated changepoint date, /level, shift, changepoint_detected verdict. test functions emit experimental cli warning treat flag potential trend change / change point, confirmed one. Use trend + change-point together: significant trend change point = slow drift; change point weak trend = one abrupt switch.
code: # Visual: rolling fan chart of the delay distribution (median, mean, 25-75 & 10-90 bands) plot_delay_drift(tn, window = 7, by_strata = FALSE, changepoint = FALSE)  # Gradual monotonic trend (autocorrelation-robust Mann-Kendall; needs `modifiedmk`) test_delay_drift(tn, stat = c("median", "spread"))   # location AND dispersion  # Abrupt shift (Pettitt change-point test; no extra dependency) test_delay_changepoint(tn, stat = c("median", "spread"))

text: batch = report date stalled desk releases backlog. moves reports later report axis without creating (mass conserved), window spanning lull + release unchanged total, whereas real epidemic surge inflates . conservation law whole method — experimental, model-free (need tbl_now), distinct epidemic surge construction. batch_test() — transport test conditions window total, size depend unknown incidence; local baseline refit report dates outside candidate window (Siegel’s repeated median, robust episode). null_model = "auto" overdispersion-aware: uses exact Poisson null non-negative counts show overdispersion (dispersion <= 1.5) otherwise dispersion-corrected robust null (always robust signed count-cumulative increments). exact Poisson null -flags overdispersed surveillance counts, prefer default; add period = 7 absorb weekly reporting cadence. BH-adjusted p-values p_transport_bh. Works count-cumulative data (reported signed increments can negative). period AUTO-RESOLVED temporal effects (v0.13.0, .batch_resolve_period): day_of_week effect -> period=7, week_of_year -> period=52 (reads get_temporal_effects(x) list; spec list(t_effects=<S7>, date_type,...), access via spec$t_effects@day_of_week). User period wins (informs disagreement). Daily data + temporal effect + period -> cli_inform suggests period=7. batch_shape_test() — one-sided rank-sum delays vs neighbouring report dates; exactly distribution-free incidence locally log-linear counts Poisson. permute = "blocks" overdispersed (NB) counts; guard omits dates adjacent (batch’s deficit sits ). simulate_batch() — closes reporting closed_dates re-stamps reports next open date; returns tbl_now. testing/teaching. diagnostic_plot(x, panels=, =) — gallery see reporting process. LAYOUT: 5 panels TWO COLUMNS (wrap_plots(ncol=2, byrow=FALSE) column-major: col1=reporting/triangle/profiles, col2=delay_drift/transport, 1 empty cell). panels (default "", exactly 5): "reporting" (reports/report date; y-axis CAPPED 99th pct via coord_cartesian dump dwarfs curve — covid_us 1.8M-report dump 2021-12-06 vs 21k median), "triangle" (event x delay; muted blue=reported zero, blank=yet reportable, FULL-calendar event axis; THIRD REPORT-DATE AXIS = dashed 45° iso-report diagonals labelled via report_ticks=6; mark_batches=0 optional), "profiles" (one delay curve per date, SINGLE colour fixed alpha), "delay_drift", "transport" (transport_discriminant() scatter, y LIMITED batch region via coord_cartesian(ylim=c(y_lo,y_hi)) WITHOUT clip=“” — clip=“” BLED panel , default clip ). Single panel → plain plot; facetted stratum; ="event" switches profiles; ... routed. panel = stand-alone exported fn (plot_reporting_process, plot_reporting_triangle, plot_delay_profiles, plot_delay_drift, plot_transport_discriminant). Reporting process = RED, epidemic process = GREEN (.diag_build_process fill keyed axis). plot_epidemic_process(x) now EXPORTED (green bars, cases event date; mirror reporting process). plot_creation_transport MOVED devel (devel/conservation_extras.R, uses tbl.now::: internals) — exported. plot_reporting_v(x) (exported, R/v_triangle.R, gallery) = reporting “V” — data plot_reporting_triangle ROTATED 45° (y=report date, left arm=event date, right arm=delay reading 0 ), batch = HORIZONTAL slice (diagonal square triangle), whole observable triangle filled w/ pale-blue zeros; coords RELATIVE ev_min (epoch nums wreck coord_fixed); arm ticks/labels/titles OUTSIDE arm, perpendicular. panels carry grey captions. EVERY plot fn takes plotly=TRUE (→ interactive plotly widget via .as_plotly/.combine_panels R/plotly_support.R; plotly Suggests). plot_scalogram(x, type=c("reporting","epidemic"), windowrad=NULL) EXPORTED (R/scalogram.R) — window-inner wavelet scalogram via wavScalogram::windowed_scalogram(sqrt(n), border_effects="INNER", energy_density=TRUE): computed OBSERVED DATA , border padding (honest “now” edge; FFT/periodic scalogram fabricates edge structure). Batch = bright SHORT-PERIOD ridge reporting (red) epidemic (green) lacks. Analysed INTEGER unit grid: dt=1 (dt=unit_days) periods come tbl’s units (weeks/days) tcentral grid INDICES; passing dt=unit_days made tcentral come back DAY-units (range 63-1043 157-week grid) → -ran date grid, dropped ~29k cells, scalogram looked empty weekly denguedat. y-label sprintf("Period (%s)", report_unit). ALSO LONG series wavScalogram SUBSAMPLES tcentral (e.g. every 5th step, 197 1095) → drawing Date axis geom_tile(width=unit_days) left 4--5 columns BLANK. Works full/filtered/daily. DEFAULTS wname="PAUL" (sharper batch localisation), windowrad=1, format="%d/%b/%y" (x-axis date fmt arg). Outside cone = panel.background=element_rect(fill="gray10") (na.value); subtitle/caption. Also: plot_transport_discriminant colours RED BH-confirmed batches (td$batch), raw per-point classification (-identifies ~10-20% alpha construction). covid_us dataset — CDC COVID-19 case surveillance, 2020-2021 events aggregated event×report (strata), built DEMONSTRATE batch reporting (huge right-skewed delay; big 2022 backlog dumps 2022-01-21 ~25× 2022-05-25 ~15×). text: Reporting delays always stable: surveillance system may speed slow season across years. plot_delay_drift() draws rolling fan chart delay distribution indexed event date — solid rolling median, dashed rolling mean, 25–75% / 10–90% quantile bands. rising falling centre line signals location drift; widening narrowing bands signal spread drift.  recent event dates time fully reported, delays look artificially short; immature region (completeness cutoff) shaded grey read drift. formal answer, test_delay_drift() runs autocorrelation-robust monotonic-trend test (modified Mann–Kendall test, via modifiedmk package) per-period delay summaries — delay series correlated , ordinary trend test -state significance. tests location statistic (median) dispersion statistic (10–90 spread), mature data : significant drift spread non-significant one median, say, mean typical delay held steady variability changed. trend test looks gradual change. instead suspect abrupt shift — reporting-system change date — use test_delay_changepoint(), applies Pettitt’s nonparametric change-point test returns estimated change date together /delay level: can mark detected change point fan chart plot_delay_drift(dengue_now, changepoint = TRUE).
